title: PRD Addendum: Identity continuity, least-privilege RBAC & key-escrow revocation flow
creator: Arjun Mehta
description: This ticket is an addendum to the Private Deploy PRD focusing on three cross-cutting enterprise requirements that surfaced during customer pilots: (1) SSO session continuity across token refresh / site-to-site federation failovers, (2) a least-privilege RBAC model for operator and support roles with scoped audit trails, and (3) a deterministic key-escrow and HSM-backed key revocation flow for customer-managed keys. The primary goal is to document clarifications, scope boundaries, acceptance criteria, and an explicit sign-off checklist so engineering and security can implement and test without rework. This addendum was scoped after two customer onboarding blockers were identified in November and January pilots. It includes concrete test scenarios, rollout constraints for Private (VPC / on-prem) installs, and mitigation plans for service continuity during key rotations and SSO provider outages.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: On a simulated identity provider outage (IdP 30s-10min), active sessions remain valid for in-flight inference requests and degrade to read-only API calls per policy; verified by end-to-end test harness (link in attachments)
SAML: Service must accept queued SAML responses after brief connectivity blips and reconcile session states without creating duplicate sessions; unit + integration tests added to CI
RBAC: All operator roles are implemented with least-privilege policies (operator, support, auditor) and role escalation requires multi-step approval recorded in audit logs

Audit logs: All SSO login events, role changes, key rotations, and escrow retrievals write tamper-evident entries to the central audit store with consistent schema and retention configurable to 7/90/365 days

KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys (CMKs) must be rotatable with an automated escrow snapshot exported to a customer-controlled vault; revocation must disable access within 30s across the control plane and inference runtime
Recovery: In event of HSM unavailability, fallback to read-only key usage mode that preserves observation-only queries and blocks new key usage until operator rekey completes
Operational runbooks: Runbook for 'IdP outage', 'key-revocation', and 'unexpected role-escalation' exist and are validated by SRE and security
Compliance evidence: Generate an evidence package (logs, config snapshots, signed attestations) for a sample onboarding customer within 48 hours of request

notes: Scope note: This addendum does not change the public API surface; it constrains runtime behavior and adds operator controls for private deployments
Trade-off: To meet 30s revocation SL, some key rotation coordination will require a temporary increase in control-plane call volume — engineering to propose batching window
Design decision: Use an escrow snapshot approach (AES-wrapped export) rather than full key duplication to minimize HSM exposure
Rollout constraint: On-prem installs require HSM firmware >= 3.4.1 and KMS operator agent 2.1+
Performance: The fallback/read-only mode will allow inference read requests only; write operations (model uploads, policy changes) blocked until rekey completes
